title: The Problem That Created Helpless Babies

scenes.script: Human babies arrive with the coordination of a badly packed nervous system.
A foal stands in hours. A human newborn cannot lift its head.
Same mammal class. Completely different launch condition.
The old explanation points to the pelvis.
Upright walking reshapes the birth canal into a narrow, twisted route.
At the same time, the human brain expands into an expensive organ.
A larger skull and a narrower exit collide in one body.
Birth moves earlier because waiting longer gets dangerous.
The baby leaves the womb before the motor system is ready.
The skull is flexible. The neck is weak. The hands cannot help.
Helplessness looks like a defect from the outside.
From the inside, it moves development into the social world.
The brain keeps wiring after birth, under faces, voices, touch, and language.
That long unfinished period changes the entire group.
One adult cannot easily feed, protect, carry, and teach for years alone.
Human childhood pulls in fathers, siblings, grandparents, and unrelated helpers.
Biologists call this cooperative breeding.
The baby becomes a social engine by being impossible to raise solo.
The cost is years of dependence.
The payoff is a brain shaped by its local world.
Other animals arrive ready for one environment.
Humans arrive ready to be trained by almost any environment.
That is why infancy lasts so long.
Culture gets time to enter the nervous system.
The useless baby is not a failed adult.
It is an unfinished brain wrapped in a body that forces cooperation.
Human helplessness is the price of human teachability.
